name: Query
first: A property wrapper that fetches SwiftData models for a view, and fetches again, and updates the view, when those models change.

dependsOn.why: A query fetches models with the model context in the view's environment.
dependsOn.whyInExample: The property `container.mainContext` is a model context, as `context` is on the page of Model context.

dependsOn.why: When the query's result changes, SwiftUI runs the body that read it again.
dependsOn.whyInExample: The `body` of `TripList` reads `trips`, as the `body` of `Counter` reads `taps` on the page of View update.

sil.shows: Reading trips reads _trips, the Query that swiftc stores for the wrapped property.

what.is: A property marked `@Query` fetches SwiftData models for a view, with the model context in the view's environment. The `body` reads the result as an array. Apple's documentation says that a query manages the models it fetched, so that they stay the same as the saved data: when matching models are inserted, changed, or deleted, the view gets the new result.
what.afterExample: The view `TripList` shows its trips, sorted by city. When line 32 inserts Cusco, the query's result changes, and the `body` runs again with all three trips.
what.problem: A list of saved trips must match what is saved: a trip added on one screen must appear on another. Fetching by hand, and fetching again after every change, is easy to forget. A query does both for the view.
what.how: Apple's documentation says that the modifier `modelContainer` puts the container, and a model context for it, in the view's environment, and that `Query` properties use that context. The query fetches the trips sorted by the key path after `sort:`. When the models change, its result changes, and SwiftUI runs the `body` that read it.

when.text: Use it in a view that shows saved models, such as a list of trips, so that the list stays the same as what is saved.
Don't use it outside a view, such as in an observable class. It needs the model context in a view's environment.

parts.name: The query `trips`, line 13
parts.text: The attribute `@Query` makes `trips` a wrapped property of `Query`, a property wrapper that SwiftData provides. Its argument `sort:` orders the trips by `city`. The wrapped value is an array of the trips it fetched.

parts.name: The modifier `modelContainer`, line 29
parts.text: The modifier puts the container in the environment of `TripList`, with a model context for it, which the query fetches with.

steps.text: Lines 20 to 25 make a container that keeps its trips in memory, and lines 27 and 28 insert two trips into its main context.
Line 29 puts the container in the environment of a `TripList`, and line 31 draws it. The query fetches the trips, sorted by city, and line 15 prints {{shows ["Lima", "Oslo"]}}.
Line 32 inserts a third trip, Cusco. The query's result now has three trips.
Line 33 runs the main run loop, and line 34 draws again. The `body` read `trips`, so it runs again, and line 15 prints {{shows ["Cusco", "Lima", "Oslo"]}}.

end.text: The query fetched the trips for the view, and when a trip was inserted, the view got the new result with no code of its own.
